title: Render documents live from source inside the app
decision: Archivist should render document views live from canonical source files at app view time. Pre-rendering should be reserved for export, print, review snapshots, or disposable caches, not the core reader model.
context: The older EPP browser pre-rendered a static review surface as part of its build style. The standalone Archivist app should preserve the old browser's visible behavior without inheriting that static-generation architecture.
rationale: Live rendering from Markdown, catalog, crosswalk, eCFR XML, artifact definitions, and workbook sidecars keeps the app local, inspectable, and current while still allowing snapshot generation for exports and reviews.
alternatives_considered: Pre-render the full EPP corpus into static HTML before browsing
Port every old artifact renderer before any full-corpus browsing
Render only simple Markdown and hide unsupported artifact blocks
consequences: Compatibility rendering means behavior parity, not static pre-rendering
Artifact work should inventory active EPP artifact blocks and provide runtime renderer support for required active families
Rare or unknown artifact blocks should degrade gracefully with source-aware placeholders until a runtime renderer exists
Export, print, and review packets may still generate snapshots from the current approved source
